status: field-source mapping diagnostic; not a site-specific SIPNET conversion

field_source.citation: Carrijo et al. 2018, Field Crops Research 222:101-110
field_source.measurement: volumetric water content at 0-15 cm depth
field_source.field_soil: 45% clay, 26% silt, 29% sand Vertisol at Biggs, California

missing_properties: field-measured site-specific saturation or field-capacity water content
model_source.external_mapping_added: site_soil_hydraulic_mapping.csv and field_site_soil_hydraulic_mapping.csv supply SSURGO surface-horizon estimates as separate diagnostics; those estimates were not inputs to the archived source runs

calculations.zero_residual_ratio: dry VWC divided by continuous-flood VWC; this assumes zero residual water and common physical support and is not asserted as the SIPNET mapping.
calculations.required_residual_vwc: theta_r = (theta_dry - fAnoxia * theta_flood) / (1 - fAnoxia); this is the residual VWC that would make the field endpoint equal the SIPNET threshold under a linear available-water mapping.
calculations.ssurgo_available_water_ratio: (theta - wfifteenbar) / awc; this is now the primary physical interpretation because SIPNET documents soilWater as plant-available water and soilWHC as its cap.

interpretation: The zero-residual dry/flood ratios remain useful as a sensitivity bound, but they are not the primary model interpretation. At the Carrijo field coordinate, SSURGO available water maps the observed AWD25 endpoint to 0.469-0.719, which contains the realized field-reference minima of 0.477-0.528. Under analogous source-site mappings, the forced 0.25 target remains above 15-bar water content but is drier than the Carrijo field observations. The archived source runs do not supply modeled depth or depth-resolved hydraulic properties, and SSURGO is mapped survey evidence rather than a run input or field measurement.
